The user is asking about the "KarstBinary 2025" result—which parts should be verified first, and why. This is a review set question. I need to find the prediction/result for "KarstBinary 2025". Let me start by loading the context to check existing projects and searching predictions.

Let's do olmoearth_load_context and olmoearth_search_predictions in parallel (they're independent).

result.models_note: These are the models in this Studio account only. Ai2 also publishes fine-tuned OlmoEarth models (the olmoearth_projects configurations and their task cards) that are not in this listing; say so instead of presenting this list as every model the user can run. prediction_type says what a model outputs: a *_regression output is a value per pixel, not a class probability and not a confidence.

facts.sentence: KarstBinary and KarstNumber were each fine-tuned in Studio on a label field of their project (train/val split 0.75/0.25), so labels for this project may exist in Studio; no tool of this run looked them up for this area.

text: Found the prediction: "KarstBinary--01-01-2025--12-31-2025--PA regular", id dd504793-1ac3-4a1c-a389-707dbaab56c5. Next, I'll retrieve its results to get the result_id and band information (since it's per_pixel_regression, a threshold is required for review_set_from_result unless the band is [0,1]).

The result is `419c581d-9a10-4684-aba5-1bab2875f26b`, and the band is "sample_karst_score". It's per-pixel regression. Need to check the declared output range — but fetch_results didn't show the declared output. Let me use olmoearth_get_prediction_result to get the declared output (range). After that, run review_set_from_result. If the band is [0,1], no threshold is needed. Otherwise, a threshold will be required.

The band is a [0,1] regression score (sample_karst_score), so I can directly use olmoearth_review_set_from_result with the default threshold behavior. Call it with grid 12 or 16 to get finer windows. Let's use grid 14 or 16 — the cap is 16. Budget defaults... The tool takes budgets as an optional array. Let me call with grid 16 and check the top few review rows.

result.assumption: The band is a score in [0, 1] decided at 0.5 and is treated as P(positive) for ranking only: each window's scores are [1 - s, s], so its margin is |2s - 1| and the least decided windows (s nearest 0.5) are opened first; the most confident windows (s near 0 or 1) come last. Ranking by distance from 0.5 needs no calibration, but these numbers are not probabilities of error, and no recorded experiment grades this case.

sampling.what_a_window_is: a grid of sampled points, not every pixel: the result's extent is cut into 16 x 16 cells and each window is ONE pixel-value sample at its cell centre, so a window stands for its cell only as far as that pixel does
sampling.nodata_rule: a sample is no-data, and is dropped before ranking, when its band is missing or NaN, equals the model's nodata_value, lies outside the band's declared regression range, or carries no class on a classification band

result.signal: margin = distance from the decision (lower = more suspect, opened first); the most confident windows come last, never first

ceiling.note: No ranking can catch more than this share of the errors at a budget; judge a realised capture against it, not against 1.0. Pass error_rate (known or estimated) for the number.

result.listing_note: review lists the first 10 of the 17 windows in the review set at budget 0.1, in review order (not a sample of them); the full list of 17, in the same order, is in the CSV review_list_b36f14e5a9.csv (rank, window_index, row, col, margin and the class or score; no coordinates); review_set_evidence.json (evidence_detail_path) holds evidence text only, no windows.

margin_summary.reading: Over all 173 windows: lowest_margin is the smallest margin (the most suspect window) and highest_margin the largest; median_margin is the middle value (half the windows lie below it), not a lower end. margin_at_budget_cut is the 17-th lowest margin (n_review at the budget); review_set is the margin range of all 17 windows in the review set, listed or not. The 163 windows ranked after the tool's 10 listed (ranks 11 to 173; not_listed) have margins from 0.580314 to 0.999842. These counts are the tool's listing's: a table of fewer than 10 rows leaves out more windows than not_listed counts, the extra ones with margins no higher than 0.580314.

result.evidence_scope: The ranking evidence (exp70 of 2imi9/olmoearth_inferenceX) was measured on OlmoEarth models' class-score margins and does not cover this case: no recorded experiment grades a regression score read as a probability.
caveats: Budgets are fractions of the valid sampled windows, not of the map's pixels.
This review set is chosen to hold errors; it is not a sample, and its error rate overstates the map's. To say how wrong the map is, use olmoearth_plan_label_sample.

facts.sentence: The median margin over all 173 windows (0.965247) is 1.69 to 12.64 times the margins of the 10 listed windows (0.076344 to 0.569681) and 1.37 to 12.64 times those of all 17 windows in the review set (0.076344 to 0.703095).

Of the 17 windows in the review set, 9 (52.9%) are predicted class 1 (above the threshold 0.5) and 8 (47.1%) class 0 (at or below the threshold 0.5); these counts cover all 17, not only the 10 listed.

must_state: No recorded experiment grades a regression score read as a probability.

forbidden_claims.why: the margin orders windows for review; it is not a probability of error, and the review set is chosen to hold errors, not sampled, so no error rate follows from it without labelling a designed sample (olmoearth_plan_label_sample)

the margin orders windows for review, least decided first; it is not a probability of error, so no window of the review set is 'most likely wrong', 'probably an error' or 'likely mislabeled', and a low margin does not say a window is more likely wrong than right, nor, since no recorded experiment grades this ranking, are they 'the likeliest spots for a wrong call' or 'the windows most likely to be wrong': call them the least decided, the most suspect or the windows to check first; which of them are wrong is known only once they are labelled

evidence_scope names upstream evidence (exp70) that the tool says does not cover this case: none of its numbers, its dataset or its finding that the margin ranks errors well applies here, neither 'in comparable cases' nor as 'upstream evidence shows'; the file at evidence_detail_path keeps that record, not a finding about this case
